stations.title: A hermitage on the hill
stations.text: Antonine hospital brothers settled on the hill of “Mont des Cats” in 1650. The French Revolution dissolved this community in 1792, and the buildings fell into ruin.

stations.title: A painter buys the ruins
stations.text: The painter Nicolas Ruyssen of Hazebrouck bought the ruins in 1819 in order to found a school there; in 1821 he opened a boarding school with the Brothers of the Christian Schools from Saint-Omer.

stations.title: Eight monks from Gard Abbey
stations.text: In 1825 Ruyssen turned to the Trappist abbey of Notre-Dame du Gard near Amiens. On January 26, 1826, eight Trappists arrived and founded Mont des Cats Abbey—still run by this community today.

stations.title: Abbey status
stations.text: In 1847 the priory was raised to an independent abbey.

stations.title: Battlefield in the First World War
stations.text: On October 12, 1914, the British 3rd Cavalry Brigade attacked German positions on the hill. The monastery was taken; the German Prince Maximilian Friedrich Wilhelm Georg of Hesse was mortally wounded and died in the abbey that same night.

stations.title: Beer to Chimay's recipe
stations.text: The abbey has no brewery of its own. In 2011 the monks presented a beer of their own, brewed to their recipe at Scourmont Abbey (Chimay)—and therefore without the “Authentic Trappist Product” seal, which requires brewing within the monastery's own walls.
